item.title: Self-Hosted Container Image Inspection Tools: Dive vs Skopeo vs crane
item.description: Container images are the fundamental building blocks of self-hosted infrastructure. Every Dockerfile produces an image composed of layered filesystems, metadata, and configuration. As teams build and maintain dozens or hundreds of container images, questions arise: How large is this image? Which layers consume the most space? Does this image contain the expected base layer? Can we verify the image signature before deploying it to production?

item.title: Self-Hosted Container Image Manifest Tools: regctl vs crane vs manifest-tool
item.description: Container image manifests define the metadata, layers, and platform compatibility of OCI container images. When working with multi-architecture images, custom registries, or supply chain security, you need tools that can inspect, manipulate, and copy image manifests across registries. This guide compares three leading open-source tools: regctl, crane, and manifest-tool.

item.title: Self-Hosted Container Garbage Collection: docker-gc vs Distribution GC vs Portainer Image Pruning
item.description: Running containers and building images over time causes disk space to balloon. Without regular cleanup, a Docker host can accumulate hundreds of dangling images, unused volumes, and stopped containers that silently consume gigabytes of storage. Container garbage collection automates this cleanup, keeping your infrastructure lean and predictable.

item.title: Self-Hosted Container Image Lifecycle: Harbor vs Distribution vs Zot (2026)
item.description: Container registries accumulate artifacts quickly. Every CI build pushes new image tags, every deployment promotes images between environments, and over time, your registry fills with outdated layers, unused tags, and orphaned manifests. Without lifecycle management, storage costs grow linearly and image discovery becomes impossible.

item.title: Self-Hosted Container Image Management: Skopeo vs ORAS vs Crane (2026)
item.description: Managing container images across registries is a daily operational task for platform engineers. Whether you’re mirroring images to an air-gapped environment, promoting builds between staging and production, or auditing what’s deployed across multiple clusters, having the right image management tooling is essential.
